organization.name: Sentara Health
organization.short_description: Sentara Health is an integrated, not-for-profit health system headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia. It includes 12 hospitals, a health plan with 1M+ members, a medical group, home health, and a college of health sciences — one of the few truly integrated delivery and financing systems in the US.

contactAnalysis.name: Michael Reagin
contactAnalysis.title: Chief Information & Technology Officer
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: CITO with dual technology and information mandate — direct authority over AI platform investments.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Present how AI unifies data across the integrated payer-provider model. Engage after champion builds internal momentum.

contactAnalysis.name: Howard Kern
contactAnalysis.title: CEO
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: CEO of an integrated system — strategic decisions about technology investments flow through here.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Executive presentation focused on 'integrated intelligence' strategic vision. Engage only after CITO buy-in and pilot results.

contactAnalysis.name: Jennifer Watts
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Digital Transformation & Innovation
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: VP Innovation is the ideal champion — actively evaluating new technologies to support Sentara's integrated model.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: First touch target. Lead with a use case specific to payer-provider integration that no standalone system can replicate.

contactAnalysis.name: Matthew Goldberg
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Data & Analytics
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Data & analytics VP would champion AI tools that enhance analytics capabilities across the integrated system.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Parallel engagement with Jennifer Watts. Focus on technical validation and data architecture alignment.

contactAnalysis.name: Laura Chang
contactAnalysis.title: Director, Health Plan Operations
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Health plan operations director evaluates AI for claims, utilization management, and member engagement — unique integrated use case.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Demonstrate payer-side AI capabilities: claims automation, risk adjustment, and member outreach optimization.

contactAnalysis.name: Brian Foster
contactAnalysis.title: Director, Clinical Informatics
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Clinical informatics bridges provider-side workflows with technology — evaluates clinical AI deployment feasibility.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Partner on clinical workflow design. He determines if AI integrates with Epic workflows across 12 hospital sites.

contactAnalysis.name: Karen Dawson
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Compliance & Risk
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Compliance VP for an integrated payer-provider system has dual regulatory scrutiny — must be addressed early.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Proactively share compliance documentation covering both payer (CMS) and provider (HIPAA/Joint Commission) requirements.

contactAnalysis.name: William Frazier
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Supply Chain & Procurement
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Post-merger procurement is consolidating vendor relationships across newly merged entities — new vendors face additional scrutiny and longer evaluation cycles.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Engage early with vendor qualification materials. Position as consolidation-friendly — one platform replacing multiple point solutions across merged entities.

plan.executiveSummary: Sentara Health is uniquely compelling because of their integrated payer-provider model — 12 hospitals and a 1M+ member health plan under one roof. Their $500M post-merger technology investment and CEO's 'integrated intelligence' strategy signal active budget deployment and executive commitment. The play is AI that spans the full payer-provider continuum — a use case no standalone payer or provider can replicate, making Sentara an unmatched case study.
plan.painToProductFit:
1. PAYER-PROVIDER DATA INTEGRATION: Both claims and clinical data in-house — AI can uniquely leverage this combined dataset for total cost of care analytics and risk adjustment.
2. POST-MERGER INTEGRATION: 12 hospitals with varying systems need AI-powered harmonization of clinical protocols and operational standardization.
3. HEALTH PLAN AUTOMATION: Claims processing, prior authorization, and utilization management for 1M+ members.
4. POPULATION HEALTH: As an integrated system bearing financial risk, AI-powered risk stratification directly impacts their bottom line.
plan.competitiveThreats: EPIC: Expanding AI within EHR may cover some clinical use cases. MICROSOFT: Azure partner with healthcare AI solutions competing for infrastructure. OPTUM/UHG: Competing integrated model with their own AI capabilities. HEALTH CATALYST: Strong analytics platform in the provider space. CONSULTING: Merger integration consultants may influence technology selection.
plan.timingUrgency: Post-merger integration means technology decisions are being made RIGHT NOW. $500M technology investment is being allocated in phases — getting in during Phase 1 is critical. Optum/UHG as an integrated competitor is investing billions in AI — Sentara must keep pace. New value-based care contracts require analytics capabilities they may not yet have.
plan.dealStrategy: Integrated model wedge strategy over 4-6 months. Phase 1: Enter through Jennifer Watts (VP Innovation) with a payer-provider integration use case. Phase 2: Parallel tracks — Matthew Goldberg for technical validation, Laura Chang for payer-side use cases. Phase 3: Show Michael Reagin (CITO) how AI unifies data across the integrated model. Phase 4: Executive presentation to CEO Howard Kern on 'integrated intelligence.' Phase 5: Pilot spanning payer and provider operations. Estimated deal size: $500K-2M initial, $5M+ enterprise. Risks: post-merger complexity, dual regulatory requirements.
plan.discoveryQuestions:
1. How are you connecting your health plan data with clinical data across the 12 hospitals?
2. What's the biggest technology challenge from the recent merger integration?
3. How does your 'integrated intelligence' strategy translate to specific AI use cases?
4. Where in the $500M technology investment is AI/analytics prioritized?
5. How does the health plan division evaluate members who are also patients in your hospitals?
plan.roiFramework: Payer-provider data fusion: AI matching claims to clinical data identifies 15-20% more risk adjustment opportunities = $150-200M revenue impact on 1M members. Total cost of care reduction: Integrated AI reducing unnecessary utilization by 5% = $500M+ savings. Clinical documentation: $45M+ annually across 12 hospitals. Claims automation: 30% reduction in manual review = $15-20M. PILOT: 90-day pilot connecting health plan risk data with clinical intervention data at 2 hospital sites.
